observations.title: An untrusted prize contract can fabricate both escrow and delivery
observations.description: The clean requirements treat arbitrary prize contracts as untrusted, but admission checks only that the contract reports ERC-721 interface support. During createRaffle, the prize contract controls safeTransferFrom: it can invoke the clone receiver with the expected caller-supplied arguments without maintaining real ownership, and the factory then asks that same untrusted contract whether the clone owns the token. This can activate a raffle with no genuine escrow. On an NFT-winning redemption, the same contract can make transferFrom a no-op and report the winner from ownerOf; the raffle then retains winnerRedeemed/prizeClaimed and the ticket burn while no genuine NFT was delivered. A sponsor controlling such a token can therefore sell entries and receive the NFT-outcome sponsor allocation without contributing an enforceable prize, contrary to the atomic-escrow and delivery requirements.
assumptions: The clean-design statement that arbitrary prize contracts are untrusted includes contracts that falsely advertise ERC-721 behavior; the interface prose's honest-prize assumption is not treated as an overriding trust assumption.
Entrants may buy from a raffle whose sponsor selected the adversarial prize contract.
The adversarial prize contract can return the ERC-721 interface ID and self-consistent but false ownerOf results while accepting transferFrom/safeTransferFrom calls.

observations.title: Clone-isolation filtering recognizes only raffles from the current factory
observations.description: Destination screening asks only this raffle's immutable factory whether an address is one of its registered clones. A clone deployed by another RaffleFactory is therefore accepted as a sponsor recipient (and can likewise be configured as a factory treasury). In a cash/refund branch, releaseSponsorPrize uses unsafe transferFrom and moves the prize into that other clone, while quote-token releases also pass the factory-local screen and become unaccounted balances in the recipient clone. The recipient clone has no rescue path. This is a concrete cross-clone asset path contrary to the stated never-move-assets-between-clones requirement, although the party selecting the destination bears the direct loss.
assumptions: More than one deployment of RaffleFactory can exist and the clone-isolation requirement applies across those deployments.
A sponsor or factory deployer selects an existing clone from another factory as sponsorRecipient or protocolTreasury.
The prize token otherwise follows ordinary ERC-721 transferFrom ownership semantics.

gaps: Source-only review: no compiler, test, fuzz, invariant, symbolic, gas, or runtime execution evidence was produced.
Gebal marked the Foundry configuration unsupported because gas_reports is an unsupported key; source intake still succeeded but compilation coverage is absent.
Docker was unavailable and no pinned local tool image was configured, so no deterministic test-inclusive plan was created and host tools were not used as a fallback.
Canonical USDC's fee-free/non-rebasing transfer semantics and the canonical Chainlink wrapper's asynchronous/authenticated behavior are trusted assumptions, not locally executed facts.
